group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 38-year-old woman arrived at the emergency department in the early evening after three days of non-productive cough, mild right-sided chest tightness, and a gradual decline in her exercise tolerance from her customary 30-minute treadmill routine to feeling winded after climbing a single flight of stairs at work. She denied shaking chills, sweats, or measurable fever at home, reporting that her highest digital oral reading had been 36.6 °C earlier that morning. Her spouse, who accompanied her, stated she had remained fully alert, paid household bills online without difficulty, and drove herself to work the entire week, but had complained of “pressure” behind the sternum when taking a deep breath. She has a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy diagnosed six years ago with the most recent outpatient echocardiogram documenting a left-ventricular ejection fraction of 40 %; her symptoms have been stable on carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, low-dose sacubitril-valsartan, and a morning 20 mg furosemide tablet that she admits she skipped yesterday because she “didn’t feel puffy.” In addition, hepatology follows her for autoimmune cholangiopathy discovered on biopsy two years prior; she takes ursodiol 600 mg daily, has normal synthetic function, and has never required paracentesis or suffered encephalopathy. She has no known kidney disorder, her last office basic metabolic panel one month ago showed a creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL, and she has never seen a nephrologist. She denies cerebrovascular accidents, malignancies, or immune-suppressing conditions. She has never smoked, drinks an occasional glass of wine on weekends, and denies illicit drug use. Vaccinations include the current season’s influenza shot given at an employer health fair and a 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate injection administered one year ago; she has not received antibiotics, corticosteroids, or inhaled bronchodilators in the past twelve months. Pre-hospital personnel transported her without intravenous fluids, oxygen, or medications so that baseline physiology could be captured. On arrival she was seated upright, speaking in full sentences, oriented to person, place, date, and situation, and answering questions briskly. Initial, untreated vital signs recorded by triage were: oral temperature 36.5 °C, pulse 90 beats per minute and regular, automated blood pressure 133/79 mm Hg confirmed manually, respiratory rate 12 breaths per minute with unlabored excursions, and fingertip pulse oximetry 93 % on ambient air at near-sea-level altitude. Skin was pink and warm with brisk capillary refill; there was no jugular venous distention beyond the patient’s baseline 4 cm vertical height and trace symmetric ankle edema identical to prior cardiology notes. Cardiac auscultation revealed a normal S1 and S2 with a faint third sound but no murmurs or rubs. Pulmonary examination demonstrated slightly diminished breath sounds at the right mid-lung field with scattered coarse crackles that cleared partially after a forceful cough; percussion remained resonant and tactile fremitus was not increased, and no dullness was elicited over the bases. The abdomen was soft with a smooth, nontender liver edge palpable 1 cm below the costal margin; no splenomegaly or ascites were appreciated. Extremities were warm without cyanosis or clubbing, and her neurologic screen—pupils, extra-ocular movements, facial symmetry, hand-grip strength, rapid alternating movements—was normal. A bedside finger-stick before intravenous cannulation measured capillary glucose at 85 mg/dL. Venous blood drawn prior to any therapy showed sodium 122 mEq/L, potassium 3.7 mEq/L, chloride 95 mEq/L, bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 44 mg/dL, creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, and hematocrit 56 % with hemoglobin 18.4 g/dL; white blood cell count was 12.6 × 10⁹/L (82 % neutrophils) and platelet count 260 × 10⁹/L. An arterial sample obtained on room air within ten minutes of arrival revealed pH 7.58, PaCO₂ 28 mm Hg, PaO₂ 83 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, indicating a primary respiratory alkalosis likely related to intermittent deeper breaths she took when chest discomfort peaked. A portable postero-anterior and lateral chest radiograph, completed before any fluids or antimicrobials, demonstrated a patchy airspace opacity in the right middle lobe with air bronchograms and preservation of both costophrenic angles, without appreciable fluid layering or obvious cardiomegaly compared with prior imaging. Electrocardiography performed concurrently showed sinus rhythm at 88 beats per minute with nonspecific T-wave flattening in V5–V6 but no acute ischemic changes and QRS duration unchanged from clinic tracings six months earlier. Two sets of peripheral blood cultures, sputum for Gram stain and culture obtained after a coached deep cough, and a nasal swab for multiplex respiratory viral PCR were sent prior to any antibiotic orders. At the moment this note is composed she remains on a regular stretcher breathing ambient air, has received no intravenous crystalloid, diuretics, antipyretics, analgesics, vasoactive agents, or supplemental oxygen beyond the small heparinized flush used for the arterial sample, and continues to converse comfortably with stable hemodynamics while awaiting admission for further management of her community-acquired lower respiratory infection.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) sums demographic, comorbidity, examination, laboratory, and radiographic points at presentation.
Demographics: for a woman, age minus 10 gives 38 − 10 = 28. No nursing-home residence: 0.
Comorbidities: chronic liver disease (biopsy-confirmed autoimmune cholangiopathy) +20; heart failure (treated cardiomyopathy with EF 40%) +10. Malignancy, cerebrovascular disease, and renal disease: 0 each.
Examination: normal mentation, respiratory rate 12 (<30), systolic BP 133 (≥90), temperature 36.5 °C (≥35 and <40), and pulse 90 (<125): 0 each.
Tests: BUN 44 mg/dL (≥30) +20; sodium 122 mEq/L (<130) +20. Arterial pH 7.58 (not <7.35), glucose 85 mg/dL (<250), hematocrit 56% (not <30%), room-air PaO₂ 83 mm Hg (not <60), and no pleural effusion: 0 each.
Total = 28 + 20 + 10 + 20 + 20 = 98 (PSI class IV).
Final answer: 98
